text:
mike_sales: Heads up — running a POC with TeraHealth. They get streaming disconnects ~30-60s and then a flood of 429s when the client retries. Need SE/Eng swarm.
anya_se: Oof. Do we know SDK versions + network path (corp proxy, WAF, TLS inspection)?
customer_engineer: ts-sdk@2.4.1, py-sdk 1.9.0. Traffic goes through BlueCoast corporate proxy with TLS inspection. Raw client shows ECONNRESET then 429s.
kevin_eng: Two likely culprits: proxy closing long-lived chunked streams OR client retry behavior not honoring Retry-After. Can you paste a short log?
mike_sales: paste from Node client: 
```
[2026-03-20T14:02:01.123Z] stream: open
[2026-03-20T14:02:31.456Z] stream: data chunk
[2026-03-20T14:03:01.789Z] error: ECONNRESET
[2026-03-20T14:03:02.001Z] retry attempt=1
[2026-03-20T14:03:02.100Z] response 429 {"error":"rate limited"}
```
lina_support: Ask them to check HTTP agent keepAlive and whether the proxy rewrites Retry-After. Many enterprise proxies close idle chunked connections after ~30-45s.
anya_se: Also whether the proxy mungs transfer-encoding or strips headers — that would break Retry-After header propagation.
customer_engineer: We see Retry-After sometimes in backend logs, but BlueCoast rewrites headers. How to make SDKs back off correctly?
kevin_eng: For TS, recommend explicit http.Agent + keepAlive and tune keepAliveMsecs. Also cap concurrent reconnects and set retry policy to jittered exponential. Example: 
```
const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 20000, maxSockets: 8 });
const client = new RedwoodClient({ requestAgent: agent, timeout: 30000, retry: { retries: 5, factor: 2, minTimeout: 500, maxTimeout: 10000, randomize: true } });
```
Key: shorter per-chunk interval (send heartbeat frames every 20s) so proxy sees traffic.
lina_support: Python: configure requests/urllib3 pooling and Retry that honors Retry-After. Example: 
```
s = requests.Session()
adapter = HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=10, pool_maxsize=10, max_retries=Retry(total=3, backoff_factor=0.5, respect_retry_after="Respect"))
s.mount("https://", adapter)
client = RedwoodClient(session=s)
```
Also enable respect_for_retry_after flag in SDK if available.
infra-bot: Note: BlueCoast defaults to drop chunked streams after 45s w/o new headers. Consider heartbeat/no-op chunks.
kevin_eng: If the proxy strips Retry-After, clients will retry immediately and hit token-based rate limits. Two-pronged approach: 1) mitigate client behavior (keepAlive, backoff, cap reconnects); 2) ask customer's infra to whitelist redwood host or preserve Retry-After.
mike_sales: Customer worried about cost: "Will retries multiply token usage?"
anya_se: Yes if full context is resent. Recommend delta/resume tokens or prefix caching. For POC, suggest checkpointing state so reconnects only send small resume token.
customer_engineer: Azure WAF might also truncate chunked Transfer-Encoding on our side. Any workaround besides changing WAF?
lina_support: Practical workaround: buffer into small content-length POSTs (batch 1-2 tokens) so proxy sees content-length and doesn't treat as long-lived chunked stream. Or fall back to short polling for POC. Not ideal for latency but stabilizes POC.
kevin_eng: I'll assemble a reproducible Node/Python sample that toggles keepAlive and retry settings + a tcpdump template and join an ENG-to-ENG Zoom to triage.
mike_sales: Action items: 1) TeraHealth to enable keepAlive and SDK backoff (ETA: EOD). 2) SEs to share Node/Python repro + packet capture template. 3) If proxy rewrites Retry-After, escalate to infra for header whitelist. I'll loop customer in.
anya_se: Ping me when they test — I can join the Zoom. :thumbsup: 
customer_engineer: Thanks all — will try changes and report tonight.
